extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced graduate students in arithmetic geometry/number theory interested in the Mochizuki/Joshi claimed proofs of the abc-conjecture
extracted.subtask_description: An FAQ-style guide describing the prerequisites, key ideas, required constructions, and essential checks needed to understand and evaluate the claimed proofs of the abc-conjecture (Mochizuki and Joshi). Focuses on Teichmüller-theoretic, p-adic, adelic, and anabelian ingredients and which mathematical objects/arguments must be established for the proofs to be complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teichmüller theory (genus one) as essential prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: (1.1) Read some classical Teichmüller Theory of genus one Riemann surfaces from any standard text on the subject (e.g. [Imayoshi and Taniguchi, 1992]). [A good understanding of the genus one case is essential.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi insists a good understanding of the genus one case is essential to grasp outlines of the claimed proof; recommends specific texts (Imayoshi & Taniguchi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand proofs of the Geometric Szpiro Conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: (1.2) Next read the proof of the Geometric Szpiro Conjecture given in [Zhang, 2001] (its approach is simpler than the prior work of [Amorós, Bogomolov, Katzarkov, and Pantev, 2000]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zhang (2001) and the geometric analyses are recommended as background since the arithmetic proof strategy mirrors the geometric case; understanding the geometric proofs is important for transferring ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teichmüller-theoretic aspects of cited geometric papers must be understood
rubrics_metrics.description: (1.3) Understanding Teichmüller Theory aspects of the above cited papers is very important. My commentary on this appears in [Joshi, 2023a, Appendix] and it shows how the principal constructs of the arithmetic case appear in the geometric case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi emphasizes mapping the principal constructs in the geometric case to the arithmetic case; his commentary expands these connections and is recommended reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector-bundle / alternate geometric approaches (Kim/Beauville)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1.4) Finally read [Kim, 2002] (or [Beauville, 2002]) which presents a different proof of the Geometric Szpiro Conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kim's vector-bundle techniques and Beauville's treatments give alternative viewpoints whose inequalities and bundle-theoretic ideas are relevant analogues in the arithmetic setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the geometric case as a model
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and prove the geometric case, and then imitate or transfer ideas of that proof to the arithmetic case. A classic example of this is the proof of Mordell’s Conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and methodological principle: geometric-to-arithmetic transfer is a standard template in Diophantine geometry and must be followed to make sense of the arithmetic argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teichmüller theory is not captured by algebraic geometry alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Teichmüller Theory deals with quasi-conformal mappings (e.g. non-holomorphic) between Riemann surfaces and these are not holomorphic and therefore not algebraic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic geometry and moduli of Riemann surfaces are necessary but not sufficient; one must understand quasi-conformal/analytic aspects that fall outside purely algebraic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct/Work with an Arithmetic Teichmüller Space
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s first key idea is to extend the analogy between Riemann Surfaces and Number Fields, and envisages a Teichmüller Theory for any fixed number field (my paper [Joshi, 2023a] independently demonstrates this idea and constructs an Arithmetic Teichmüller Space for each fixed number field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The arithmetic proof requires a bona fide arithmetic Teichmüller space (local and global versions) whose points parametrize distinct 'arithmetical holomorphic structures' — understanding its construction and properties is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averaging/integrating over Teichmüller/Arithmetic Teichmüller spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s second key idea (very roughly speaking) is to average over the Teichmüller Theory of a Number Field (in [Joshi, 2024c], [Joshi, 2024b] the averaging is over the Arithmetic Teichmüller Space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averaging integrals over Teichmüller-type spaces (analogous to classical Teichmüller integrals) is a central analytic/measure-theoretic step and must be made precise; examples in Wright (2019) show similar techniques in the geometric case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with p-adic untilts and non-topologically-isomorphic perfectoid fields K
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists an algebraically closed, complete valued field K containing an isometric embedding of Qp, such that K ≃ Cp as abstract algebraically closed fields but K and Cp are not topologically isomorphic and hence not isomorphic as (complete) valued fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The arithmetic Teichmüller viewpoint requires recognizing and using untilts K distinct from Cp; these provide distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures and allow valuation deformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Fargues–Fontaine curves as p-adic Teichmüller spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The view of [Joshi, 2023a] is that Fargues-Fontaine curves constructed in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018] are the Teichmüller space for finite extensions of Qp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using Fargues-Fontaine geometry to parametrize untilts and arithmetic holomorphic structures is a foundational geometric identification for the arithmetic theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tempered fundamental groups and track geometric base-points
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempered fundamental groups ... are pro-discrete groups and capture infinite discrete coverings such as that of Tate elliptic curves, while étale fundamental groups work with finite étale coverings. The tempered fundamental group requires one to work with Berkovich spaces. The datum of geometric base-points consists of algebraically closed complete valued fields (containing Qp isometrically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof strategy requires tempered (not just étale) fundamental groups and explicit tracking of geometric base-points (untilts); these base-points label distinct versions of arithmetic and are mathematically significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with all geometric base-points extends the object (arithmetic loop spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working with all geometric base-points is tantamount to working with an extended object ... this set contains X(C((T ))) which is the algebraic loop-space of X, and it strictly contains X(C) (in general).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One must consider the full family of geometric base-points/untilts (holomorphoids) to obtain the enlarged arithmetic object used for averaging and comparison arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation scaling / Teichmüller dilatations must exist and be non-trivial
rubrics_metrics.description: This scaling of valuations ... is precisely the sort of relationship Mochizuki asserts ... Mochizuki sometimes refers to this sort of valuation scaling property as 'Teichmüller dilatations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nontrivial valuation-scaling phenomenon across untilts is a critical analytic ingredient; establishing its existence is nontrivial and central to the inequality-estimates in the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product formula acts as the global glue across primes
rubrics_metrics.description: You really want to do this over all primes and use the product formula as a global glue. The product formula for number fields provides global gluing in the arithmetic case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local analyses at each p are combined using the product formula and adelic/global structures; any global bound must incorporate the product formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and explicit construction of a global Frobenius (log-Link)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a global Frobenius morphism φL : (cid:89)L → (cid:89)L ... This mapping is a precise version of the Log-Link considered in [Mochizuki, 2021b, Page 32].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A global Frobenius that simultaneously twists valuations at all primes, allows Frobenius-twisted comparisons, and plays the role of Mochizuki’s log-Link is needed; Joshi constructs such a morphism and shows how it is used in inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of adelic methods and global multiplicative actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adelic constructions are typically built using local objects and then one uses some global glue to glue all the local pieces together ... the product formula ... and (1) the global action of the multiplicative group of a number field ... (2) the action of a global Frobenius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The arithmetic proof framework must combine local untilt-level data via adelic spaces, multiplicative group symmetries, and the global Frobenius to obtain global inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish non-trivial symmetries: Galois action, Θ-Links, log-Links
rubrics_metrics.description: The second difficulty is to demonstrate the existence and non-triviality of various symmetries (Galois action, Θ-Links, log-Links/global Frobenius) asserted by Mochizuki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness requires explicit, intrinsic geometric demonstrations that these symmetries exist and act as required; Joshi claims to produce these properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate existence of distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures (avoid meta-universes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working with distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures is absolutely necessary ... My approach provides a canonical way to disambiguate Mochizuki’s claims about arithmetic holomorphic structures and avoids any discussion of ∈-loops or any meta-mathematical considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central requirement is to construct (rather than posit) distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures (holomorphoids/untilts) and show they can be distinguished without recourse to set-theoretic universes or meta-mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Berkovich analytic spaces (and Huber/Spa functors) rather than pure schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: My approach ... abandons working with schemes and works with Berkovich rigid analytic spaces and arrives at a more intrinsic p-adic notion ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling the analytic/arithmetic holomorphic structures via Berkovich spaces (and relating to Scholze's diamonds X♢ via Huber's functor) is a recommended technical framework to realize the required structures concretely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct local holomorphoids and link them to Scholze's X♢ (explicit labeling of base-points)
rubrics_metrics.description: A point of the local Arithmetic Teichmüller Space Holy(X) consists of an untilt of C♭p, a geometric base-point ∗Ky : M(Ky) → XanQp ... Holy(X) also arises ... from some x ∈ X♢(C♭p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof framework requires explicit local objects (holomorphoids) that keep track of base-points and map naturally to Scholze's diamond formalism; these labeled objects are the units over which averaging/comparison is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare Tate parameters across different arithmetic versions via Ainf or Galois cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two approaches ... One using Galois cohomology (pioneered by Mochizuki) and a second approach using the rings Ainf,p = W(OC♭p) ⊂ Bp considered in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018]. Both approaches are essentially equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compare Tate parameters qE;y computed in different untilts/holomorphoids one must use either Galois-cohomological identifications or Teichmüller-lift techniques via Ainf; making these comparisons explicit is necessary for global bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarge the set of objects (Θ → Θ′) by varying arithmetic avatars to obtain tractable volume bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s idea ... is to carefully choose a subset S of arithmeticoids and enlarge Θ to Θ′ by taking qE;y for y ∈ S and estimate the size of Θ′ instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strategy replaces a hard-to-bound original family with an enlarged family (by varying arithmetic versions) whose volume/height can be estimated, thereby obtaining bounds for the original family indirectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate geometric product relations to arithmetic product formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: In the geometric case of [Zhang, 2001] ... the fundamental group relation plays the role of the product formula for number fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing the precise arithmetic analogue of geometric product/monodromy relations is necessary; understanding how the product formula appears in the geometric proofs guides the arithmetic construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness criterion for a proof: must provide explicit constructions for key ingredients (distinct holomorphic structures, Frobenius/log-Link, averaging) rather than relying on opaque toolkit usage
rubrics_metrics.description: My assertion of incompleteness is based on the genuine difficulty one encounters in using Mochizuki’s toolkit in proving his assertions. The central difficulty is to show that there exist distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures ... The second difficulty is to demonstrate the existence and non-triviality of various symmetries ... I prove these properties from an intrinsic geometric point of view in my papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid/complete proof must explicitly construct and verify the existence/nontriviality of the arithmetic Teichmüller space, valuation scalings, global Frobenius/log-Link, and the symmetries used in averaging; merely asserting these ingredients without construction is treated as incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on set-theoretic universes/∈-loops in core arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s Key Principle of Inter-Universality ... suggests treating geometric base-points as belonging to distinct universes. Joshi: 'I do not agree with the assertion that all the needed meta-mathematics is carefully worked out ... one can in fact avoid this meta-mathematical conversation by carefully establishing the existence of distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete mathematical constructions (untilts, Fargues-Fontaine points, holomorphoids) which render universes/unorthodox set-theory unnecessary in the main body of the proof; this is part of Joshi's completeness test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use global arithmetic objects (arithmeticoids, complete adelic curves, global valued fields) for further applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each arithmeticoid ... naturally provides a complete adelic curve in the sense of [Chen and Moriwaki, 2020] ... also provides a global valued field in the sense of [Yaacov et al., 2024].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructing arithmetic Teichmüller spaces yields structures that connect to adelic-curve and global-valued-field frameworks, indicating further checks/corollaries to validate the constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate and verify analogues of vector-bundle Frobenius inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The inequalities proved [in geometric Kim/Beauville] are very similar to the bundle theoretic inequalities proved using the genuine Frobenius morphism for vector bundles proved in [Joshi and Pauly, 2015].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of verifying the arithmetic inequalities required for abc is to reproduce/transplant vector-bundle/Frobenius destabilization inequalities in the arithmetic/adelic setting or show precise analogues.
